title: Sausage Plait
subtitle: A puff pastry plait with herbed sausagemeat filling
excerpt: Seasoned sausagemeat wrapped in puff pastry and scored to look like a plait, then baked until golden. Good for buffets, packed lunches and picnics.
sourceNotes: British bakery classic, adapted for a standard baking tray using shop-bought puff pastry.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unbaked or baked. Reheat a baked plait from frozen at 180C for 20 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the plait, cover with cling film and chill for up to a day before baking.

content.text: A sausage plait is a large sausage roll with its sides cut into strips and folded over in a criss-cross pattern. The effect is impressive and the technique is straightforward. Use sausagemeat rather than whole sausages so the filling is smooth and holds together when sliced.
Heat the oven to 200C and line the baking tray with baking paper.
Mix the sausagemeat, grated onion, sage, mustard and black pepper together in a bowl until well combined.
Unroll the pastry sheet on the lined baking tray. Shape the sausagemeat into a log down the centre third of the pastry, leaving about 4cm clear at each short end.
Cut the pastry on either side of the filling into strips about 2cm wide at an angle. Fold the short ends up over the filling first.
Fold the strips alternately over the filling, left then right, pressing lightly so they stick. This creates the plait effect.
Brush all over with beaten egg. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the filling is cooked through. Rest for 5 minutes before slicing.

items.symptom: The plait opens up during baking.
items.cause: The strips were not pressed firmly enough onto the filling.
items.fix: Press each strip down firmly as you go. Brush with egg before baking, which also acts as glue.

items.symptom: The filling is undercooked in the centre.
items.cause: The sausagemeat log was too thick.
items.fix: Keep the filling log no wider than 6cm so the heat reaches the centre in the baking time.

items.cause: Fat from the sausagemeat pooled under the pastry.
items.fix: Use baking paper and place the tray in the upper third of the oven so the base gets direct heat.
